cards.title: Sequence an ecommerce advertorial around the next buyer objection
cards.summary: When cold traffic needs product education before reaching the purchase page.
cards.use_when: When cold traffic needs product education before reaching the purchase page.
steps: Map ad promise, hook, researched customer situation, alternatives, product mechanism, proof, objections, price and guarantee in that order as a starting structure.
Make each section answer the question raised by the preceding section.
Identify the page as advertising and carry the same angle from ad to page to product offer.
Test against the existing product-page journey using purchases, acquisition cost and contribution margin.
caveats: Source conversion and revenue figures are case claims, not benchmarks.
Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Align the cold-traffic ad with the advertorial hook
cards.summary: When ad clicks do not turn into engaged product-page visitors.
cards.use_when: When ad clicks do not turn into engaged product-page visitors.
steps: Choose one researched shopper problem and a supportable product benefit.
Let the ad introduce a specific question that the page answers promptly.
Match the audience, promise and tone in the opening headline; do not borrow the source example medical claims.
Test alternative hooks while holding the downstream offer stable.
caveats: Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Write a specific product-use story from customer research
cards.summary: When an advertorial describes abstract benefits instead of a recognizable buying situation.
cards.use_when: When an advertorial describes abstract benefits instead of a recognizable buying situation.
steps: Identify the practical moment that creates demand: the task, place, friction and desired outcome.
Use authentic customer language and observed details rather than invented personal testimony.
Show how the product changes that moment, then connect to the next objection.
If presenting a real customer story, preserve its actual limitations and permission.
caveats: Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Compare real alternatives before explaining product differentiation
cards.summary: When shoppers see the product as interchangeable with cheaper alternatives.
cards.use_when: When shoppers see the product as interchangeable with cheaper alternatives.
steps: List the alternatives customers actually consider, including keeping the current solution.
Compare relevant limitations using accurate features, total cost, compatibility or effort.
Explain the specific tradeoff the product addresses and acknowledge who may prefer another option.
Avoid unsupported competitor failures or claims that retail products replace professional treatment.
caveats: Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Explain a supported product mechanism before the offer
cards.summary: When the buyer needs to understand why product features address their problem.
cards.use_when: When the buyer needs to understand why product features address their problem.
steps: Identify a genuine, supportable cause of the practical product-use problem.
Connect each relevant feature to that problem with a clear explanation or demonstration.
Use specifications only when verified for the actual SKU; label uncertainty where evidence is limited.
Move to proof and the offer once the buyer can explain the connection.
caveats: The source medical root-cause and percentage examples are not reusable evidence. Do not invent an expert or proprietary scientific cause.
Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Match authentic product reviews to purchase objections
cards.summary: When shoppers need proof relevant to fit, use, value or reliability.
cards.use_when: When shoppers need proof relevant to fit, use, value or reliability.
steps: List the major buying objections and find genuine reviews addressing each.
Preserve the customer wording and actual result; do not write testimonial personas.
Use real usage timelines only where documented, without promising the same result to everyone.
Answer remaining delivery, compatibility and returns questions in the FAQ.
caveats: Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Reveal the price against a defensible product comparison
cards.summary: When the advertorial must explain value before the purchase CTA.
cards.use_when: When the advertorial must explain value before the purchase CTA.
steps: Use a genuine comparable product, bundle contents or total ownership cost as the anchor.
Show the actual price, quantity, recurring charges if any, and delivery costs clearly.
Use a compare-at price or stock deadline only when accurate.
Place a guarantee the merchant can honor beside the CTA with its relevant terms.
caveats: Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Close an advertorial with useful questions and genuine proof
cards.summary: When the bottom of the page leaves shoppers unsure about ordering.
cards.use_when: When the bottom of the page leaves shoppers unsure about ordering.
steps: Recap the product benefit, what is included, price and purchase action.
Answer real shipping, gifting, stock and returns questions.
Display authentic customer comments if available, or clearly label merchant-written answers as an FAQ.
Check that the CTA leads to the promised SKU and offer.
caveats: Do not fabricate comment threads, customer avatars or expert endorsements.
Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.
